claims.claim: Starship Flight 14 targets a 275 km altitude orbit for six orbits over nearly 10 hours.
claims.episode_span: The mission targets a 275 km altitude orbit where the upper stage will complete six orbits over nearly 10 hours before Pacific splashdown.
claims.source_title: SpaceX's Starship is about to attempt a 10-hour spaceflight: Watch live.
claims.supporting_quote: The plan is to send Starship around the planet six times before splashing down in the Pacific Ocean to the west of Chile.

claims.claim: The upper stage will reach orbital velocity of approximately 7.8 km per second on Flight 14.
claims.episode_span: Reaching orbital velocity of approximately 7.8 km per second changes the mission profile because the vehicle must now actively de-orbit after hours of operation.
claims.source_title: Starship Flight 14 Aims for Full Orbital Insertion, First Deployment of 26 V3 Satellites Over Six Orbits
claims.supporting_quote: a spacecraft must reach a velocity of approximately 7.8 kilometers per second to remain in orbit.

claims.claim: Booster B1100 completed its tenth flight and landing on the USSF-385 mission.
claims.episode_span: The Falcon 9 booster B1100 flew its tenth mission on the USSF-385 launch and landed on the droneship Of Course I Still Love You 35 days after its previous flight.
claims.supporting_quote: Booster B1100 landed on Of Course I Still Love You for its tenth flight and tenth successful landing

claims.claim: USSF-385 marked the fourth classified Space Force launch from the same Vandenberg pad in roughly six weeks.
claims.episode_span: USSF-385 was the fourth classified Space Force mission from the same Vandenberg pad in roughly six weeks, following USSF-366 on August 15, USSF-153 on September 10, and USSF-259 on September 17.
claims.source_title: 4th USSF Launch in 6 Weeks Speeds Starshield Buildout, X Report 27 Sep 2026
claims.supporting_quote: marking the fourth Space Force launch from the same pad in roughly six weeks.
